summary: Shuman Chen works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned her PhD from Northwestern University by 2014, studying under doctoral supervisor Brook Ziporyn and traditional teacher Weijue Shi.

Shuming Liang (1893–1988) was a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. After attending Shuntian Middle School (~1906–1911), he joined Peking University's philosophy department in 1917 and later founded the Shandong Rural Reconstruction Institute and China Democratic League.

Shun'ei Hirai (b. 1930) is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at Komazawa University (~1949–1953) and the University of Tokyo (~1953–1974), later serving at Komazawa University as professor (1964–1976), vice president (1986–1990), and emeritus professor (2001).

Shun'ei Mori is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. He held posts at Ryukoku University (attested 1990) and as a part-time lecturer at Chikushi Jogakuen Junior College (attested 1995).

Shunkyo Katsumata (1909–1994) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1932–1935). He held posts at Toyo University and Taisho University (~1943–1980), where he became emeritus professor.
Shunpaku Nakao is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served on the faculty at Shuchiin University, where he was an assistant professor (attested 1963) and later professor (attested 1976).

Shunpei Ueyama (1921–2012) studied philosophy and Japanology at Kyoto University (1941–1943). He taught at Kyoto University (assistant professor 1954, professor 1968, emeritus 1982–1984) and headed the Kyoto National Museum (~1988–1995) and Kyoto City University of Arts (~1995–1999).

Shunryu Suzuki (1904–1971) was a Buddhist teacher who studied at Komazawa University (1925–1930) and Eihei-ji. He served as abbot at Zoun-in, Rinsō-in, and Soko-ji, and founded the San Francisco Zen Center and Tassajara Zen Mountain Center.

Shunshō Manabe (b. 1939) works in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Tohoku University (~1963–1969) and held posts at Hosen Gakuen College and Shikoku University, serving as professor at the latter (~1995).

Shunsuke Tsurumi (1922–2015) was a philosopher who studied at Harvard University (~1939–1942) under Willard Van Orman Quine. He held academic posts at Kyoto University (~1954–1960), Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1960–1961), and Doshisha University (~1961–1970).
Shuntaro Kondo (b. 1974) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Ryukoku University in 2011 and worked there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2012).

Shuntarō Matsuyama (1930–2014) specialized in Indology and religious studies. After studying under Naoshiro Tsuji at the University of Tokyo (graduating in 1951 and 1953), he lectured at several institutions and was a professor at Joshibi University of Art and Design (~1972–1996).

Shunzo Onoda is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a D.Lit. from Bukkyo University in 1993 and later served there as associate professor (attested 1996) and professor (attested 2005).

Shuyu Kanaoka (1927–2009) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1952) and Toyo University (~1957–1962), later serving as an assistant professor at Toyo University (~1969–1992).

Shwe Zan Aung (1871–1932) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a B.A. from the University of Rangoon (~1888–1891) and studied under traditional teachers U Gandama and Ledi Sayadaw in 1895.

Shōdō Yamagami (b. 1939) specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. After doctoral studies at Kyoto University (~1962–1964), he served at Kyoto Sangyo University as assistant professor (~1974–1989) and professor (~1989–2010).
Shōkō Kabutogi (1912–1985) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Rissho University (~1932–1936) and later returned there as a professor (~1964–1982).
Shūei Tsuboi (1914–1989) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a professor at Bukkyo University (attested 1963, 1972) and was an editorial committee member for The Bukkyo Bunka Kenkyu.

Shūichi Katō (1919–2008) studied at the University of Tokyo (Dr. med. 1950) and worked in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Sophia University, University of British Columbia, Ritsumeikan University, and several European and American institutions.

Si Ti La is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Acharya Nagarjuna University under J. Sitaramamma. He also studied under several traditional teachers, including Sayadaw U Kundala and U Sajjanasāra.
